Detect consecutive repeated measurements

Source: R/Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats.R
Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats.Rd

`r lifecycle::badge("experimental")`

Counts, per subject, the rolling windows of `nWindowLength` consecutive measurements in which every value is identical. Missing values are dropped before windows are formed. Records are ordered by `strDateCol` within subject, then by `strOrderCol` to break same-date ties.

Usage

Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats(
  df,
  strValueCol,
  strSubjectCol = "subjid",
  strDateCol = "vs_dt",
  strOrderCol = NULL,
  strMeasureCol = NULL,
  strMeasureVal = NULL,
  nWindowLength = 3
)

Arguments

df

`data.frame` One row per measurement record.

strValueCol

`character` Column holding the measurement value.

strSubjectCol

`character` Subject identifier column. Default `"subjid"`.

strDateCol

`character` Date/ordering column. Default `"vs_dt"`.

strOrderCol

`character` Optional column(s) used, in order, to break ties on `strDateCol` (e.g. an intra-visit measurement time or `"visit"`). Default `NULL`, in which case tied records keep their input order.

strMeasureCol

`character` Optional column identifying the measure, for long-format data. When supplied, `df` is filtered to `strMeasureVal`.

strMeasureVal

`character` Value of `strMeasureCol` to keep. Required when `strMeasureCol` is supplied.

nWindowLength

`numeric` Window length; a whole number >= 2. Default `3`.

Value

A `data.frame` with one row per subject in `df` (after measure filtering): the subject column, `Numerator` (count of all-equal windows), and `Denominator` (`n - nWindowLength + 1`, floored at 0, where `n` is the subject's non-missing measurement count). Subjects with a `Denominator` of 0 contribute nothing to a rate.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  subjid = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5),
  vs_dt = rep(as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:4, 2),
  weight = c(10, 10, 5, 3, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10)
)
Detect_ConsecutiveRepeats(df, "weight")
#>   subjid Numerator Denominator
#> 1      A         0           3
#> 2      B         3           3
